title: Tolland wins Section 4 Little League championship, honoring late teammate in the process - NewsBreak
text:
COVENTRY — The scoreboard at Miller Richardson Field only began to tell the story of the Tolland team's march to the Section 4 Little League Baseball title and a spot in the upcoming state tournament . The 21-2 victory over AWSM (Ashford-Willingford-Stafford-Mansfield) on Wednesday night was just starting to sink in as the players gathered for a team photo underneath the scoreboard. However, everybody waited until the Tolland No. 1 jersey was included in the group shot. There was no way a photo could be taken without a memory of a fallen teammate. That was the uniform wore by AJ Salisbury, a teammate and friend of the victorious Tolland team. It was just over 15 months ago that cancer claimed the life of the 10-year-old AJ. AJ's father was in attendance with not only his son's jersey, the last batting glove he wore but also his ashes in a cup that read #AJ Strong, #HookC (in honor of his connection with the UConn baseball program ) and the Los Angeles Dodgers, his favorite team. "It is beyond anything I could even think of," said Fernando Hernandez, AJ's father. "It still takes my collective breath away. "I can't even put into words what this means to our family. You never recover from this but this helps with the healing." It would be easy to say that AJ Salisbury would have been on the Section 4 championship team. The reality is that every player and coach affiliated with the team knows that he is still a part of them. "He is still with us, he has always been with us," said outfielder Nicky Bucchere, who had a three-run triple and scored three runs in the title game. Tolland renamed its Little League field in AJ's honor. Fittingly, the District 8 championship was won by Tolland on AJ Salisbury Memorial Field. "When he passed away, it affected the whole community," said winning pitcher Jack Palozie, who put Tolland in front with a three-run home run. "It just feels amazing to go to states and honor him because he loved baseball and he is being honored." AWSM took the early 2-0 lead with two hits, a walk and three wild pitches in the first inning. It stayed that way until Tolland scored 11 runs in the fourth inning and added 10 more in the fifth inning. Every player scored at least one run for Tolland. Palozie drove in four runs, Kai Locke had three hits as did Harrison Skinner. Palozie pitched the first three innings, he allowed two hits and had four strikeouts. Jaxson Dumas only gave up one hit in the final two innings. "It means everything," Tolland manager Scott Biondi said. "His spirit was watching over us. It was special and it made it extra special. For a town our size to be able to go down there, I can't wait for these boys to get their chance to shine on that stage." Bobby Tantillo had two hits to lead AWSM. Now Tolland heads to the state tournament as one of the final four teams in contention to represent Connecticut in the Eastern Regional. AJ's family will be in attendance every step of the way. "All we have are the memories now and this is a great memory," Hernandez said. "I hope they run with it." at Coventry AWSM 200 00-2 3 2
